cuts.reason: Cuts from the wide dual-shot establishing the restaurant table straight into an extreme close-up on the woman's deadpan face right as the dialogue starts ('You've been sighing at this menu'), punching in for her guilty reaction and revealing the 'MENU' word-caption gag.
Cuts to an extreme close-up on the other character's chin/collar as the line 'Everything has truffle on it' lands, isolating the word with a 'TRUFFLE' caption pop for comedic emphasis.
Jumps back to the woman's face on 'Just pick something,' a quick punch-in that mirrors the earlier reaction shot and keeps the back-and-forth bickering rhythm tight.
Cuts to an extreme close-up on the man's furious, wide-eyed face exactly as he objects with '$29,' timing the cut to the anger beat of the objection line.
Cuts back to the woman's flat, judgmental close-up to deliver the punchline word 'famous,' holding on her unimpressed expression for the joke's landing.
Hard cut to black title/end card revealing the series branding ('Low Battery People, created by Nin, New Episode Daily') as the CTA button after the punchline.

reaction_shots.description: Close-up on the woman's tired, deadpan face while being called out for sighing over the menu; 'MENU' caption overlay.
Quick close-up on the woman's unimpressed face reacting to being told to 'just pick something.'
Extreme close-up on the man's angry, flustered face mid-objection about paying $29 for the mushroom.
Close-up on the woman's flat, sarcastic expression delivering the 'mushroom that got famous' punchline.

pacing_notes: Opens with a slower ~2.6s wide establishing shot of the couple at the table, then settles into a tight shot-reverse-shot rhythm of ~2s extreme close-ups alternating between the two characters, each synced to a word-caption pop (MENU, TRUFFLE, SOMETHING, $29, FAMOUS). The shortest shot (~1.2s) lands on the terse line 'Just pick something,' tightening pace right before the objection and punchline beats, which each hold slightly longer (~2s and ~1.9s) to let the reactions land. The video then cuts to a distinct final black title/CTA card (~1.4s) for series branding, breaking the visual rhythm to signal the button/outro.
